clue.text: Boats from Liverpool sound

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for Liverpudlian is to be said out loud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: Scouse describes someone or something from Liverpool, a port city in north-west England

explanation.surface: Vessels heard in the port of Liverpool, or a sound of water near the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noun for a stretch of water by Liverpool; it signals a homophone. SCOUSE (the Liverpool accent or person) is said like the flat-bottomed boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Scows are flat-bottomed barges used for carrying cargo.

clue.text: Journalist dined out of carafe, being overcome

parts.note: a sub, short for sub-editor, is a newspaper journalist
a jug is a carafe for serving water or wine
dined means ate

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer drinks too much from the wine carafe at dinner and is overwhelmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces sit side by side in answer order: the journalist, the carafe, then the dining; 'out of' and 'being' only link them.
explanation.definitionFit: To subjugate is to conquer or bring under control, the verb sense of overcome.

clue.text: Carmen, for example, work over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Bizet's opera singer is made to work extra hours.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'over-time' at a line break; read as 'over time', the work sits on top of the time in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmen is Bizet's best-known stage work set to music, an instance of the art form.

clue.text: Bones that may appear at a feast

definitions.text: Bones that may appear at a feast

parts.words: Bones that may appear at a feast
parts.note: the frame of bones in a body, and the proverbial gloomy presence at a celebration, the 'spectre at the feast'

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'the skeleton at the feast' means someone or something that spoils an otherwise happy occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A full set of bones is a body's framework, and the idiom puts such a reminder of death at a banquet.

clue.text: Llamas moving round watering hole in Spanish province

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the next piece
moving says the letters of the animals' name are to be shifted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange
a spa is a resort with mineral springs, a place to take the waters

explanation.surface: Llamas wander about a water hole somewhere in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' reorders the animals' letters to give LALMAS, and 'round' splits those letters around the spa. 'watering hole' looks like a bar but is a spa town.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Palmas is a province of the Canary Islands, an autonomous region of Spain.

clue.text: Cement needed for the instrument

definitions.meaning: a clay or paste used to seal joints, a kind of cement
a plucked stringed instrument with a pear-shaped body

explanation.surface: A builder's cement turns out to be essential for a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: a sealing clay used by chemists and potters, and a Renaissance plucked string instrument.

clue.text: Music is played during take-off here

definitions.text: Music is played during take-off here

parts.words: Music is played during take-off here
parts.note: take-off reads as an aircraft leaving the ground but means taking off clothes, with music accompanying the act

explanation.walkthrough: 'take-off' suggests an airport; the removing is of garments, on stage, to music.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque act in which a performer undresses slowly to music.

clue.text: Squadron leader has gone off gliding, feeling sick

indicators.note: has gone off says one piece leaves the word for gliding

parts.note: sailing is gliding smoothly along, as through the water or air

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Squadron

explanation.surface: An RAF squadron leader is grounded from gliding because he feels unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squadron leader' looks like an RAF rank; it is just the letter S, which leaves SAILING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ailing is in poor health, unwell.

clue.text: Negotiate to staff the whole works

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it
an oeuvre is the entire body of work of an artist or writer

explanation.surface: Bargaining to put workers into the entire factory.
explanation.walkthrough: OEUVRE is the French-derived word for an artist's complete output.
explanation.definitionFit: To manoeuvre around an obstacle is to steer a way past it, as one might negotiate a bend.

clue.text: Son is on the wagon — he's in love

indicators.note: in a down clue, is on puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm wagon

explanation.surface: A son who has stopped drinking turns out to be smitten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the wagon' means teetotal, but here the wagon is a WAIN, with S on top of it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a poetic word for a young lover or suitor.

clue.text: Complaint by scoffer to warder

parts.note: a beef is slang for a grievance or complaint
to scoff is to eat greedily, so a scoffer is an eater

explanation.surface: A guard is grumbling about a man who mocks him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffer' suggests a mocker, but it means someone who wolfs food. BEEFEATERS are the Yeoman Warders who guard the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeater is the popular name for a Yeoman Warder at the Tower of London.

clue.text: Notice nothing about this girl…

indicators.note: about says the notice and the nothing together are turned round

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Nobody pays any attention to a certain young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole run ADNIL backwards. The girl's name continues into the next clue via the ellipsis.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a woman's first name, so a fair stand-in for a girl.

clue.text: … nothing daunted, she married

parts.note: Una is a girl's name, so stands for 'she'
wed means married

explanation.surface: Continuing the story: undeterred, the girl went ahead and married.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the girl in the previous clue; 'she' is another girl's name, UNA.
explanation.definitionFit: To be not at all daunted is to be unafraid, without any awe.

clue.text: Be a parasite, and stink in the nose when found out

indicators.note: in says the smell goes inside the rearranged letters
found out suggests exposure, but here it says the letters of the word for the snout are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange
pong is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A freeloader is caught, and the stench of discovery fills the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found out' reorders the nose's letters to give SEON, and 'in' sets the stink inside. 'stink' is the British slang PONG.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge on someone is to live off them without giving back, like a parasite on a host.

clue.text: Asking for a bill, a tester, should be above this

definitions.text: Asking for a bill, a tester, should be above this

parts.words: Asking for a bill, a tester, should be above this
parts.note: a bed whose canopy, called a tester, stands above it on corner columns; 'asking for a bill' plays on 'for poster', a bill being a poster

explanation.walkthrough: A tester is the canopy over a bed, carried on four posts; the opening also suggests a request 'for poster', a bill being a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed with tall corner columns that carry a canopy overhead.

clue.text: One who looks to heaven for guidance

definitions.text: One who looks to heaven for guidance

parts.words: One who looks to heaven for guidance
parts.note: seems to describe a pious believer praying, but the guidance is read from the stars and planets

explanation.walkthrough: 'heaven' suggests prayer; the person reads the sky's planets and stars to forecast events.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who claims to foretell events from the positions of stars and planets.

clue.text: The proboscis, by the way, is possibly A 1

parts.note: an elephant's proboscis is its trunk
a road is a way

explanation.surface: An elephant's trunk, incidentally, might be first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A 1' looks like 'first-class', but the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, from London to Edinburgh, a main through route.
explanation.definitionFit: Trunk roads are Britain's major arterial highways, of which the A1 is an example.

clue.text: Acknowledge a solemn promise

parts.note: a vow is a solemn promise

explanation.surface: Making a solemn pledge is an admission.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow something is to declare or admit it openly.

clue.text: Women's Institute's opposed to evil state

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women, with the 's kept
con means against, as in pros and cons
sin is wickedness, evil

explanation.surface: The Women's Institute stands against wickedness in the land.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British village women's society famous for jam and good works.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisconsin is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Keep one's distance from a footballer

definitions.meaning: a ... half is a rugby football player, also called fly-half

explanation.surface: Avoiding a football player.
explanation.walkthrough: The footballer plays rugby football: the stand-off (fly-half) links the scrum-half and the backs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to stay aloof, and as a noun names the rugby position between the scrum-half and the three-quarters.

clue.text: A small case of pins and needles

definitions.text: A small case of pins and needles

parts.words: A small case of pins and needles
parts.note: reads as a mild tingling in a limb, but means a little box holding sewing items

explanation.walkthrough: 'pins and needles' suggests the tingling sensation; it is literal sewing kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental container for needles, pins and similar items.

clue.text: Angry elders, for example, are supporters of the stick

parts.note: cross means angry
elder is a kind of tree, so elders are examples of trees

explanation.surface: Irate old people back the use of the cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elders' suggests older people and 'stick' a cane; the elder is a tree and the stick is a ship's mast, held up by crosstrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosstrees are horizontal spars at a masthead that brace the rigging, so they support the mast.

clue.text: Terrifying woman would need public relations to get on

indicators.note: would need says this piece lacks the next one, which must be restored to make the word for getting on

parts.note: to progress is to get on, advance

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman would have to hire a spin doctor to succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus PR makes PROGRESS (get on); so it is PROGRESS with PR removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a frightening monstrous woman.

clue.text: Fulfil promise and create capital

parts.note: to make is to create
capital as an exclamation means excellent, good

explanation.surface: Keep a promise and raise money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money, but here it is the old-fashioned 'Capital!' meaning splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good is to succeed or to carry out what was promised.

clue.text: Magnate has under a second to pull up

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the second piece below the first

parts.note: mo, short for moment, is a second

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word for pull is read from the bottom

parts.note: to lug is to pull or drag

explanation.surface: A tycoon has less than a second to stop his car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LUG to GUL in this down entry, and 'under' sets it beneath MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful, wealthy person, like a business tycoon.

clue.text: Popular wisecrack — nothing blue

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
a dig is a pointed remark, a jibe
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A well-liked joke but nothing smutty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' suggests risqué humour, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep shade between violet and the colour of the sky.

clue.text: Twice-nightly showing of "The Tribesmen"

indicators.note: showing of says letters are on display inside the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A theatre advertises two performances a night of a play called The Tribesmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside twICE-NIghtly. The Iceni were the ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a tribe of ancient Britons in what is now East Anglia.

clue.text: Approve the wine after it's been opened

indicators.note: opened says the wine loses its opening letter, as a bottle loses its cork

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian dessert wine

explanation.surface: A taster gives the nod to the wine once it has been uncorked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opened' looks like uncorking; it removes T from TOKAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To okay something is to give it the go-ahead, sanction it.

clue.text: Wood is in the musical dictionary

definitions.meaning: ... Dictionary of Music and Musicians is the standard reference work on music

explanation.surface: The conductor Henry Wood appears in the music reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Wood, founder of the Proms, would indeed be in Grove's Dictionary, which is the surface trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A grove is a small group of trees, and Grove is the familiar name for the great music encyclopedia.

clue.text: Bids for control to collar the bowling

parts.note: to collar is to seize or take
in cricket the bowling is delivered in overs, sets of six balls

explanation.surface: Attempts to seize the attack in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls bowled from one end in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Takeover bids are attempts to gain control of a company.

clue.text: Drunken salt ready to be tempted into sin

indicators.note: drunken says the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tipsy sailor is ready to be lured into wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like a sailor, but its letters are fodder with READY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone led astray has been lured into wrongdoing.

clue.text: Pretend to be willing to speak

indicators.note: to speak says the word for willing is said out loud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: fain is an old word for glad or willing

explanation.surface: Faking eagerness to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIN, archaic for 'gladly willing', is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign is to put on a false show, to fake.
